title: Titanium Bone Plate
alloyReason: Ti-6Al-4V ELI (Extra Low Interstitials, ASTM F136 / ISO 5832-3) is the medical-grade standard for permanent implantable devices. Its lower oxygen (<0.13%) and iron (<0.25%) content provides superior fracture toughness and fatigue resistance compared to standard Grade 5, making it mandatory for orthopedic and spinal implants.
commonFailures: Surface contamination from iron pickup during machining requiring acid passivation (ASTM F86)
Thread damage from improper installation torque exceeding recommended values
Galvanic corrosion at interface with dissimilar metals in electrolyte environments

faq.q: What is a titanium bone plate?
faq.a: A titanium bone plate is a precision-machined trauma fixation component used in modular locking compression bone plate. Manufactured from Ti-6Al-4V ELI (ASTM F136) for optimal strength, corrosion resistance, and weight savings.

faq.q: What standards apply to titanium bone plate?
faq.a: Titanium Bone Plate is manufactured to ASTM F136 / ISO 5832-3 (Ti-6Al-4V ELI) or ASTM F1295 (Ti-6Al-7Nb) for medical implants. This requires oxygen <0.13%, iron <0.25%, and 100% traceability with MTC per batch.

faq.q: How is titanium bone plate manufactured?
faq.a: Titanium Bone Plate is manufactured using VAR melting. Critical process controls include tool path optimization, coolant temperature management, and dimensional verification at each operation.

faq.q: What is the most common issue with titanium bone plate?
faq.a: The most common issue is surface contamination from iron pickup during machining requiring acid passivation (astm f86). Mitigation includes proper process control, material certification, and adherence to recommended installation procedures and torque values.

faq.q: What is the lead time for titanium bone plate?
faq.a: Standard lead time: 2-4 weeks depending on quantity and complexity. Rush orders available. Contact our team with your drawing and quantity for an accurate delivery quote.
